citations.assessment: The Mishnah and Bavli name Rabbi Yose be-Rabbi Yehudah on a partition consisting of only warp or woof.
The baraita explicitly distinguishes Rabbi’s disqualification of wooden vessels from Rabbi Yose bar Yehudah’s permission.
Yose bar Yehudah adds leather cutters to the craftsmen allowed before noon.
Yose explicitly requires work with both hands and feet.
Yose requires theft from both parents in the wayward-son case.
In 2:3 Yose treats the enemy as forewarned, while 2:6 gives his preliminary flight rule. Yehudah has separately attributed rulings in both units.
In 2:3 Yose treats the enemy as forewarned, while 2:6 gives his preliminary flight rule. Yehudah has separately attributed rulings in both units.
The page reproduces and examines both named opinions in their respective contexts.
Yose requires the minimum thread-width throughout a majority of the ring. The ensuing legal assessment limits that ruling to the large ring.
The same unit explicitly distinguishes the plain Yose from Yose bar Yehudah, who applies a north-south split on the altar.
Mishnah 8:7 and the exact Bavli parallel at 87a name Yose bar Yehudah on wine with floating particles. The received page 63a has a distinct Yose HaGelili discussion. Keep the discrepancy visible.
Yose accepts the count where ten were taken from a hundred or one from ten.
Yose distinguishes inadvertent substitution from the case of consecrated animals.
The Mishnah calls him his son in the garlic-vow clause. Nedarim 62a explicitly names Yose bar Yehudah but on the folded-cutters episode. Preserve the two distinct content correspondences.
Yose bar Yehudah relates the Sidon case and the Sages’ dispensation after the vow and divorce.
Both Rabbi and Yose bar Yehudah are named in the encounter on the road. Yose explains his conduct by the example of Jacob.
The baraita explicitly gives the three admonitions of Yose bar Yehudah to Rabbi.

Sifrei 335 places Rabbenu’s arrival from Ladikya before the appearance of Yose and Elazar. The checked digital form omits the additional abbreviated person’s arrival, which remains visible in Heilprin.
The Bavli calls Yose bar Yehudah Setimaah in one report and excludes him in another. Rashi explains the label as one whose views Rabbi accepted repeatedly and taught anonymously.
The Bavli explicitly names him transmitting Rabbi Eliezer’s view.
The baraita gives the distinct warning procedure in Rabbi Eliezer’s name.
The Tosefta parallel uses Rabbi Elazar in the checked witness, different from Bavli Rabbi Eliezer.
The Tosefta pairs Yose’s own position on removing dirt with a separate one transmitted in Rabbi Eliezer’s name, a reading different from the collective rendering Elazar.
Yose and Rabbi Elazar be-Rabbi Shimon both deem the slaughter effective in removing impurity.
The same two sages explicitly require a full twenty-four-hour window for annulment of vows.
Yose, Yonatan ben Yosef and Shimon ben Menasya offer distinct scriptural premises for overriding Sabbath restrictions to save life.
The two named sages disagree about liability to tithe the produce in question.
The exact passage distinguishes the two Yose occurrences in the immersion discussion.
The answer invokes Rabbi Yose be-Rabbi Yehudah’s position on immersion delayed to the final time.
The response distinguishes the specific Yose bar Yehudah in explaining why a learned person does not require warning.
Tosafot reaches the opposite identification for that distinct case because Meir is the colleague and disputant.
Akiva, Yose bar Yehudah and Shimon ben Azzai appear in consecutive statements about tithing dates in this unit.
The witnessed term appears in 51b, where Yose and Elazar be-Rabbi Shimon are mutually alternative attributions. The parallel starts near the next folio, so note the received 51a and link 51b.
Yose bar Yehudah and Elazar bar Yose both transmit the opinion that a son and daughter are equal in inheritance from their mother.
The two positions are explicitly assigned to Yehudah and his son at adjacent points in Gittin 4:7. Identity of every unqualified Yehudah cannot be inferred from this one passage.
The Yerushalmi gives the direct reply on the walls of Shushan. The ensuing sugya explains how their results can agree while their derivations differ.
